<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|220|THE GOSPEL|CHA. II.}}</noinclude>{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. II.}}}}}}

{{c|''At the request of his mother he vvorketh his first miracle, turning vvater into vvine at a mariage in Galilee, although the time of his manifestation be not yet come. 12 Then in Hierusalem at Pasche, being but one, and yet obscure, he throweth out of the Temple most miraculously al the marchantes. 28 And being yet of the blind Iewes asked a signe, he signifieth so long before, that they should kill him, but he wil rise againe the third day. 23 Which also presently they vvould doe, but that he knovving their falses hartes (though many beleeue in him) vvil not tarie among them.''}} {{dropinitial|A|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial A, two satyrs.png|imgsize=185px|fl={{verse|chapter=2|verse=1}}}}ND {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō the 2 Sunday after the Epiphanie.}}the third day there vvas a mariage made in Cana of Galilee: and the mother of {{sc|Iesvs}} vvas there. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=2}}† And {{sup|‖}} {{sc|Iesvs}} also vvas called, and his Disciples to the mariage. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=3}}† And the vvine failing, the mother of {{sc|Iesvs}} saith to him, {{sup|‖}} They haue no vvine. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=4}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} saith to her, {{sup|‖}} VVhat is to me and thee vvoman? my houre commeth not yet. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=5}}† His mother saith to the ministers, {{sup|‖}} VVhatsoeuer he shal say to you, doe ye. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=6}}† And there were set there sixe water-pottes of stone, according to the purification of the Ievves, holding euery one tvvo or three measures. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=7}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} saith to them, Fil the vvater-pottes vvith vvater. And they filled them vp to the toppe. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=8}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} saith to them, Dravv novv, and carie to the cheefe stevvard. And they caried it. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=9}}† And after the cheefe stevvard tasted the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ He that seeth water turned in to wine, nedeth not dispute or doubt hovv Christ changed bread into his body.}}∷ vvater made vvine, and knevv not vvhence it vvas, but the ministers knew that had dravvne the vvater: the cheefe stevvard calleth the bridegrome, {{verse|chapter=2|verse=10}}† and saith to him, Euery man first setteth the good vvine: and vvhen they haue vvel drunke, then that vvhich is vvorse. But thou hast kept the good vvine vntil novv. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=11}}† This beginning of miracles did {{sc|Iesvs}} in Cana of Galilee: and he manifested his glorie, and his Disciples beleeued in him.⊣

{{verse|chapter=2|verse=12}}† After this he vvent dovvne to Capharnaum him self and his mother, and his brethren, and his disciples: and there they remained not many daies. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=13}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō Munday in the fourth weeke of Lent.}}And the Pasche of the Iewes vvas at hand, and {{sc|Iesvs}} vvent vp to Hierusalem: {{verse|chapter=2|verse=14}}† and he found in the temple them that sold oxen and sheepe and doues, and the bankers sitting. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=15}}† And vvhen he had made as it vvere a vvhippe of litle coardes, he {{sup|‖}} cast them al out of the temple, the sheepe also and the oxen, and the money of the bankers he powred out, and the tables he ouerthrevv. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=16}}† And to them that sold doues, he said, Take avvay<noinclude>{{rh|||these}}</noinclude>
